jobs.description: Character: the exact PLAGUE DOCTOR creature in Image 1: long ivory beaked mask, round black lenses with tiny amber glints, black worn brimmed hat with burgundy band and bronze brooch, charcoal tattered cape, purple-black curling tentacles with pale suckers. Preserve hat, beak, costume and tentacles across all twelve poses.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / game sprite animation atlas.
Make a transparent-background production sprite atlas of ONE creature in TWELVE different fully assembled animation poses. Exactly FOUR columns by THREE rows, equal sized cells, landscape sheet. Every cell contains the whole creature, not separate components. Keep generous transparent gutters. No labels, captions, grid lines, scenery, shadows or background of any color. Genuine alpha transparency. No detached decorations. Maintain IDENTICAL character design, palette, pixel density, head size and costume details in every frame. All heads face LEFT; no mirrored frames.
Image 1 is the approved CHARACTER DESIGN reference: preserve it faithfully, including recognizable ornaments and materials; no redesign. Image 2 is the old octopus animation atlas: use ONLY its bottom three rows as the pose and movement reference, NOT its purple character design or top component rows. Render the new character in the same detailed crisp pixel art as Image 1, suitable for downsampling into a 134 by 86 pixel frame. Use fairly low/wide octopus poses, not tall portrait poses. Do not simplify the design into a generic octopus.
Pose order, reading left to right:
Row 1: (1) idle hover, head upright, arms gently spread and curling below; (2) swim pulse, arms gathered underneath, compact forward-thrust pose; (3) glide, head faces left and arms stream horizontally RIGHT; (4) curled turn, limbs tightly curled around the underside.
Row 2: (5) rest on sand, body lowered, arms spread in a low resting fan; (6) crawl reach, front arms reach LEFT along ground, rear arms trail; (7) crawl push, arms gather to push body forward, head lifted slightly; (8) settled rest, head lowered and limbs curled compactly under it.
Row 3: (9) active swim pulse, arms strongly gathered and body lifted; (10) active glide, limbs fully extended horizontally RIGHT behind the head; (11) active crawl reach, front arms extend LEFT strongly and rear arms curve; (12) active curled turn, tight compact tucked limbs.
Each cell is a DIFFERENT pose but the head/costume remains the same size. Position head/mantle near the horizontal center of each cell; allow arms to reach left or right. Keep full hats, fins, ribbons and limbs inside their own cell with visible empty padding. Head stays at consistent scale throughout, no variable zoom.
Character: the exact PLAGUE DOCTOR creature in Image 1: long ivory beaked mask, round black lenses with tiny amber glints, black worn brimmed hat with burgundy band and bronze brooch, charcoal tattered cape, purple-black curling tentacles with pale suckers. Preserve hat, beak, costume and tentacles across all twelve poses.

jobs.description: Image 1 is a four-concept board. Use ONLY the bottom-right character labeled 4 — Possessed doll. Ignore the other three designs entirely. Preserve its cracked porcelain side-profile doll face, small dark red glowing eye, black lace bonnet with burgundy ribbon and bronze brooch, black lace collar, dark wooden articulated tendrils and torn velvet ribbons. Make TWELVE poses of THIS SAME doll creature only. No human body or legs; its octopus-shaped limbs remain wooden marionette tendrils.
